edits.text:
SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT — NONBINDING DISCUSSION DRAFT
Subject to contract and Seller approval. This draft records proposed terms only and creates no obligation to sell, buy or consummate the transaction unless and until definitive documentation is executed. Any existing confidentiality agreement remains unaffected.

1. Purchase Price and Payment. The Seller proposes a base purchase price of USD 45,000,000 for the Shares on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital. The Buyer’s USD 35,000,000 counterproposal has not been accepted. The definitive agreement shall specify the treatment of cash, indebtedness, debt-like items and transaction expenses, an agreed normalized working-capital target and accounting policies, and completion-account adjustments without double counting. An estimated Closing payment shall be reconciled against completion accounts through agreed preparation and objection deadlines, mutual access to supporting records and determination of unresolved accounting items by an independent accountant acting as expert. Payment shall be by wire transfer of immediately available funds, subject only to any expressly agreed escrow and legally required withholding. Seller account instructions shall be authenticated before payment; initial instructions and any subsequent changes must be independently verified through a previously established contact using independently verified contact details, and not solely by reply to the communication providing the instructions.

2. Diligence, Closing Conditions and Interim Conduct. The Buyer shall complete its financial, tax, legal and commercial diligence before signing definitive documentation; there shall be no post-signing subjective diligence or financing condition. Closing shall occur promptly following satisfaction or lawful waiver by the party entitled to its benefit of the agreed conditions, with a target of 30 days after signing. The Seller proposes an outside date of 60 days after signing, subject to an expressly agreed extension mechanism for outstanding regulatory approvals. Conditions shall include required regulatory and identified material third-party approvals; release at Closing of encumbrances over the Shares; delivery of customary share-transfer documents, corporate authorizations and payment; accuracy of fundamental warranties in all material respects and of other warranties subject to an agreed material-adverse-effect standard, with appropriate treatment of existing materiality qualifications and date-specific warranties; material compliance with interim covenants; and absence of a material adverse change under an agreed definition. That definition shall exclude general economic, market and industry changes, changes in law or accounting standards and effects of the announcement of the transaction, with a negotiated disproportionate-impact exception where appropriate. The parties shall use agreed reasonable efforts to secure approvals and satisfy conditions. Either party may terminate if Closing has not occurred by the outside date, unless its own material breach caused the failure to close; the definitive agreement shall also provide termination rights for a final legal prohibition and an uncured material breach preventing satisfaction of a Closing condition, with appropriate notice and cure periods. Termination shall preserve accrued rights for prior breach and expressly surviving obligations.
Between signing and Closing, the Seller shall procure operation of the business in the ordinary course in all material respects. Except as disclosed and agreed, required by law or expressly contemplated by the definitive agreement, distributions, new indebtedness outside agreed ordinary-course limits and material transactions outside the ordinary course shall require Buyer consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. The Buyer shall receive reasonable information access on notice, subject to confidentiality, privilege, applicable law and noninterference with the business; access shall not confer pre-Closing operational control.

3. Warranties, Disclosure and Claims. The definitive agreement shall contain negotiated Seller warranties addressing authority and enforceability; ownership of and title to the Shares; capitalization; financial statements and undisclosed liabilities; taxes; material contracts; litigation; legal compliance; employment; intellectual property; and insolvency. Business warranties shall be subject to appropriate, specifically negotiated knowledge and materiality qualifications and matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail in disclosure schedules delivered and agreed before signing. Post-signing disclosures shall not automatically cure a breach or qualify a Closing condition without the Buyer’s agreement. The Seller shall coordinate preparation of the disclosure schedules alongside pre-signing diligence, subject to privilege, confidentiality and applicable law.
The definitive agreement shall provide contractual remedies for warranty breaches, a negotiated pre-Closing tax indemnity and any specifically agreed diligence-related indemnities. The Seller proposes an 18-month survival period for general business warranties, a general warranty liability cap of 10% of the final purchase price and an aggregate deductible basket of 1%, with a per-claim de minimis threshold to be agreed. Fundamental warranty claims shall be subject to a separate cap not exceeding the final purchase price and an agreed longer survival period; tax claims shall have separately agreed limitations and survival tied to the applicable statutory period. Any fraud exception shall be carefully defined and shall not limit liability that cannot lawfully be limited. The Seller proposes an escrow of 5% of the Closing purchase price for 18 months, credited against and not additional to applicable liability caps, with release of the balance at expiry except for reasonably quantified amounts relating to properly notified outstanding claims. No additional holdback is proposed. Claims provisions shall address notice, defense and settlement of third-party claims, mitigation, recoveries under insurance or from third parties, and prevention of double recovery. Contractual remedies shall be exclusive to the extent permitted by law, subject to agreed fraud and equitable-relief exceptions. These limitations, escrow terms and survival periods remain proposals for negotiation, not agreed terms.

4. Confidentiality and Announcements. The definitive agreement shall require each party to keep confidential the transaction terms, negotiations and nonpublic information received in connection with the transaction, subject to customary exclusions for information lawfully public or independently obtained without breach of duty. Disclosure shall be permitted on a need-to-know basis to professional advisers and, for the Buyer, its affiliates, prospective financing sources and their advisers, provided recipients are bound by professional duties or contractual confidentiality obligations appropriate to the information and no less protective in substance. Each disclosing party shall be responsible for breaches by its permitted recipients, subject to any expressly agreed exception for recipients directly bound to the other party. Disclosure may also be made with the other party’s prior written consent or to the extent required by applicable law, regulation or legal process. Where legally permitted, the disclosing party shall give prompt prior notice, cooperate reasonably in seeking confidential treatment and disclose only what is required. Public announcements shall require prior agreement on timing and content, except where legally required, in which case the announcing party shall consult the other party in advance where legally permitted. Existing binding confidentiality obligations remain in force pending execution of definitive documentation.

receiver.requested_changes:
1. Price: Replace the proposed USD 45,000,000 base price with Buyer’s USD 35,000,000 proposal, subject to satisfactory pre-signing diligence, agreed adjustments and definitive documentation. Specify the equity-price bridge and prohibit double counting across cash, debt, debt-like items, transaction expenses and working capital.

2. Working capital and completion accounts: Set the target using average monthly normalized operating working capital over the latest 12 completed months, tested against a 24-month history for seasonality and recent trading. Define included accounts and normalizations in an agreed illustrative schedule. Exclude cash, financing debt, income-tax balances and Seller transaction expenses to the extent separately accounted for. Address aged receivables, inventory obsolescence, accruals and deferred revenue expressly. Apply agreed transaction-specific policies first, then consistent historical policies to the extent compliant with the agreed accounting framework. Provide a dollar-for-dollar adjustment, an estimated statement five business days before Closing, Buyer’s completion accounts within 90 days after Closing and Seller’s objections within 30 days after receipt. Allow 20 business days to resolve objections before referring only disputed accounting items to an independent accountant; legal interpretation disputes remain for the agreed dispute forum. Provide reciprocal records access and prompt payment after final determination.

3. Prioritized diligence: First priority is three years of annual financial statements, 24 months of monthly management accounts and working-capital schedules, current year-to-date trading and budget comparisons, quality-of-earnings information, cash and debt schedules, receivables/payables aging, inventory reserves, transaction expenses and contingent or off-balance-sheet liabilities. In parallel, request capitalization and title records, shareholder arrangements, liens, material customer and supplier contracts, change-of-control consents, regulatory approvals, tax returns and audits, litigation and compliance matters. Next request employment and benefit arrangements, IP ownership and licensing, cybersecurity/privacy matters, insurance, property and environmental information where relevant, and draft disclosure schedules. Privileged or restricted materials should be identified by category and addressed through lawful alternatives, redaction or clean-team arrangements, without requiring privilege waiver.

4. Closing: Accept the 30-day target and 60-day outside date in principle, with an agreed regulatory extension. No post-signing subjective diligence condition is needed if diligence and schedules are completed before signing. Any commitment without a financing condition requires Buyer approval and funding readiness before signing. Fundamental warranties should be accurate in all respects, save immaterial inaccuracies where appropriate; other warranties should be brought down in all material respects without duplicative materiality qualifiers, rather than only to a material-adverse-effect threshold. Require releases of agreed business liens and debt payoff documentation as well as clean title to the Shares.

5. Interim protections: Prohibit distributions, value leakage, related-party transfers and extraordinary indebtedness without express Buyer consent. Apply a reasonable-consent standard to appropriate ordinary commercial matters, not automatic permission for leakage. Preserve lawful pre-Closing operational independence.

6. Remedies: Buyer proposes 24-month general warranty survival, a 20% general cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and no separate de minimis pending review of claim exposure. Fundamental warranties should have a purchase-price cap and six-year survival, subject to applicable law; tax survival should extend 60 days beyond the relevant statutory assessment period, including extensions. Tax and specific indemnities should sit outside the general warranty basket and cap, with their own agreed limits. Seek a 10% escrow for 24 months, preserving reasonably quantified pending claims and direct recourse against Seller for liabilities exceeding escrow. Escrow is security, not a separate liability cap. Preserve legally available fraud remedies and appropriate equitable relief. Timely notified claims must survive until resolved, and delayed notice should bar recovery only to the extent of material prejudice.

7. Documentation: Add governing law, dispute forum, notices and customary definitive-agreement provisions. Retain authenticated payment instructions, agreed pre-signing disclosure schedules and the rule against unilateral post-signing cure. All proposals remain nonbinding pending Buyer approval and execution.

Thank you. The revised draft provides a useful basis for further discussion. Buyer maintains its USD 35,000,000 base-price proposal on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital. We cannot support USD 45,000,000 on the information supplied. Please provide the financial and valuation support for that position and indicate whether Seller is prepared to negotiate from it. Buyer’s proposal remains subject to diligence, agreed risk allocation, Buyer approval and definitive documentation.

Our immediate diligence priorities are: (i) three years of annual financials and 24 months of monthly accounts, current trading and budget comparisons; (ii) monthly working-capital detail, receivables/payables aging and inventory reserves; (iii) cash, indebtedness, debt-like liabilities and transaction expenses; (iv) capitalization, share title and liens; and (v) material contracts and consents, tax exposures, litigation and regulatory matters. Please also provide a timetable for the remaining legal, employment, IP, privacy and operational materials and draft disclosure schedules. We acknowledge that none have yet been delivered. Controlled disclosure and lawful privilege protections are acceptable; please identify restrictions so alternatives can be arranged.

For working capital, we propose a latest-12-month normalized monthly average, tested against a 24-month history for seasonality and recent trading, with agreed account definitions, policies and a worked example before signing. Adjustments should be dollar-for-dollar and avoid duplication with debt, cash or expenses. Buyer would prepare completion accounts within 90 days, Seller would have 30 days to object, and unresolved accounting items would go to an independent accountant after a short resolution period.

We can work toward the proposed closing timetable, with a regulatory extension mechanism. Diligence and disclosure schedules must be completed before signing; acceptance of no financing condition remains subject to Buyer approval and funding readiness. We require a stronger warranty bring-down than the proposed MAE threshold and appropriate payoff and lien-release deliveries.

On remedies, our counterproposal is 24-month general survival, a 20% general cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and 10% escrow for 24 months. Fundamental, tax and identified diligence risks require separate treatment, with direct Seller recourse beyond the escrow and appropriate fraud protections. We also require express protection against pre-Closing leakage.

Please confirm Seller’s willingness to engage on price and these principal protections, and propose a data-room delivery schedule. All positions remain nonbinding and subject to definitive agreement.
